title: AuthSystem
subtitle: Login done properly
description: A complete authentication service: email verification, password resets, refresh-token rotation and Google/GitHub OAuth, with emails and OTPs handled on a background queue instead of blocking the request.

sections.heading: WHY THIS EXISTS
sections.content: Every project I built needed auth, and every time I copy-pasted a half-baked JWT setup. I wanted one service I actually trusted, built once and reused, with real token rotation and OAuth done properly instead of bolted on.

sections.heading: THE HARD PART
sections.content: Handling refresh tokens safely without hammering the database on every request. I designed it around token families with reuse detection, so a stolen or replayed refresh token invalidates the whole family instead of quietly slipping through.

sections.heading: WHAT CHANGED IN MY HEAD
sections.content: Security isn't a feature you bolt on. The difference between a toy auth system and a real one is in the edge cases — what happens when a token gets reused, when an OAuth account already exists under a different provider, when an email job fails. That's now just part of how I build anything.

sections.heading: WORTH POINTING AT
bulletPoints: Refresh token rotation with reuse detection across token families
Google and GitHub OAuth via the server-side authorization code flow, not client-side ID tokens
Atomic OAuth account resolution using a database transaction, so a signup can't half-complete
Email verification, password reset, and OTPs handled through BullMQ background jobs
Fully Dockerized with Redis for sessions and an admin dashboard
